summary: Feature A (Sub-Admin Preview) and Feature B (per-site timezone + per-order tz rendering) both verified end-to-end. Backend pytest 5/6 pass — only failure is a benign data assertion that legacy sites in the DB lack an explicit 'timezone' field (frontend still defaults to Asia/Kolkata per spec). Frontend: (A) Eye button opens sub-admin-preview-modal with preview-nav (Home + Vendor Onboarding + Sales + Feedback + Menu Requests), preview-permissions (4 labels), scope block, preview-effective-sites (2) — ZERO POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE fired while modal was open (read-only confirmed); preview-close-btn closes it cleanly. (B) New-Site modal has site-timezone-input defaulting Asia/Kolkata; per-card site-timezone-select-{id} PATCHes /api/sites/{id} and persists across reload (round-tripped NY→Europe/London→NY successfully). (B) Per-order tz rendering: same UTC instant 2026-09-09T13:42:07Z renders as '09:42:07 am' for CRV-AUDA01 (NY) and '07:12:07 pm' for CRV-AUDB01 (IST) on BOTH /vendor/all-orders AND /vendor/orders — proves order.site_timezone is honored across panels. No 5:30 IST drift regression.

minor.issue: Legacy sites (5 of 11) returned without a 'timezone' field in the JSON. Frontend falls back to Asia/Kolkata so display is correct, but for API consumers/tests it would be safer to serialize a default 'Asia/Kolkata' when the field is absent (single-line coalesce in the site serializer).

action_items: Optional: default missing site.timezone to 'Asia/Kolkata' in the /api/sites list serializer for API-consumer robustness (frontend already defaults, so this is cosmetic).
critical_code_review_comments: Preview modal is genuinely read-only — zero write calls observed. Good separation from an 'impersonate' feature.

Per-order site_timezone attach in orders.py uses a bulk sites->tz map (good, no N+1). Same pattern in vendor_reports.all_outlets_orders. Consider hoisting into a shared helper (utils/site_tz.py) — currently duplicated between two routers.
AllOrders.js / Orders.js now pass explicit timeZone option to toLocaleString(). The earlier iter-71 comment (no explicit timezone) is addressed for these three panels.
Sites GET does not backfill a default 'timezone' for docs written before the field existed; either backfill script or coalesce in serializer would clean up ambiguity.

success_rate.backend: 83% (5/6 tests; the 1 failure is a strict-schema check, not a functional bug)
